name: Importance-Driven Volume Rendering
definition: A technique for automatic focus and context display of volumetric data that generalizes cut-away views. It assigns an object importance to each part of the volumetric data to encode visibility priority, determining which structures are readily discernible and which are less important. Objects occluding more important structures are displayed more sparsely, while objects in areas with no occlusion are rendered densely.
summary: Importance-Driven Volume Rendering dynamically adjusts opacity based on viewpoint-dependent occlusion to keep important features visible while suppressing less important ones.
